title: Package page on your phone: pick a layout
question: You open a package from the Telegram link. Flags come first, then Approve. Which layout should the package page use? (Colors and fonts stay Air Check's; only the arrangement differs.)

options.label: Checklist, then approve
options.thesis: Every review flag is a line you acknowledge; Approve unlocks only when nothing is left unread.
options.viewport: Phone. Header strip with show date and status. 'For your review: 2 flags' list with a tick circle per flag. Collapsed rows for Title, Description, Tracklist (31). Player bar with Jump to hour 2. Sticky bottom: 'This will be public on Mixcloud' and a green Approve that is disabled until both flags are ticked, with Edit and Skip beside it.
options.risk: Ticking can feel like busywork when flags are trivial.

options.label: What Air Check changed
options.thesis: Show the agent's work as before-and-after pairs, so trust comes from seeing each change and its reason.
options.viewport: Phone. 'What changed' section first: Drive 'Ly Qua Dub' → Paper 'Lý Qua Dub', 'Left out of description: pre-air verify list (unverified)', 'Left out: one personal detail (handle with care)'. Each row has a source label (Drive / Paper / Notes). Then the public title and description, tracklist, player bar, sticky Approve / Edit / Skip with the public warning.
options.risk: Longer page; the decision sits further down.

options.label: One-screen decision
options.thesis: Everything needed to decide fits one phone screen; details are one tap away.
options.viewport: Phone. One card: serif title, tags row, '31 tracks · 2 closing · 5 tags', the two flags as short lines, 'See everything' link, player bar, then three large stacked buttons: Approve (green), Edit, Skip, with 'This will be public on Mixcloud' above them.
options.risk: Hides the tracklist and description behind a tap.
